paper.title_en: Cosmic Web Dependence of Neighboring Dark Matter Halos around Low-mass Hosts in the TNG50 Simulation
paper.abstract_en: We investigate whether the population and radial kinematics of neighboring dark matter halos around low-mass hosts differ between filament and sheet environments in the TNG50 cosmological hydrodynamical simulation at z = 0. We select host halos with 11.0 ≤ log ,10 ,( M ,200 c ,/ [ M ,⊙ , h ,− 1 ,] ) < 11.5 and construct 192 filament-sheet host pairs closely matched in host mass and local density. An all-pair host-companion cross-correlation shows that the clustering around filament hosts is stronger than that around sheet hosts by 0.16 ± 0.06 dex over 2 < R/R$_{200c}$≤ 4, corresponding to a factor of about 1.5. The same qualitative enhancement is recovered when using comoving separations rather than distances scaled by R$_{200c}$, and the integrated contrast remains positive in the spatial-block jackknife realizations. In contrast, the median peculiar radial velocities are broadly similar between environments, and the inward-motion fraction becomes lower around filament hosts beyond approximately 3R$_{200c}$. Filament hosts therefore possess a significantly richer neighboring-halo population than closely matched sheet hosts, while this excess is not accompanied by stronger coherent radial infall. The clustering enhancement remains robust to variations in the companion-mass threshold and to substantially tighter host mass and local density matching. These results support a persistent association between cosmic web environment and the neighboring-halo reservoir around low-mass hosts in TNG50.
